In this case report, we present four cases of the implantation of the Aveir VR in the atrium of male pediatric patients to treat sinus node dysfunction. Retrospective review of patients with symptomatic sinus node dysfunction and atrially placed Aveir-VRs was performed at UC Davis between April 2024 and April 2026. Femoral access was the route of implantation for all 5 patients. Trans-esophageal echocardiography was used in all cases. The patients' ages ranged between 14-17-years and follow-up appointments were held between 1-23-months. Immediately post-procedure, impedances were 380-1460 Ohms, thresholds at 0.4 ms were 2.25-3.5 V, and P-waves were between 1.7-3 mV. Follow-up impedance was between 390-720 Ohms for the patients, thresholds were 0.5-1.25 V at 0.2-0.4 ms, P-waves were between 4.5-9.1 mV, and pacing percentages were between 12-69%. This case series demonstrates the successful implant of Aveir VR leadless pacemaker in five young patients for sinus node dysfunction.

title: The "Reverse Break" Pattern in Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome: A Rare Electrocardiographic Marker for Right Posteroseptal Accessory Pathways
summary: Background: The surface electrocardiogram (ECG) remains the cornerstone for localizing accessory pathways (APs) in WolffParkinson-White (WPW) syndrome prior to catheter ablation. The "reverse break" (or double transition) pattern in the precordial leads is a uniquely rare and highly specific finding for posteroseptal pathways. Case Presentation: A 60-year-old female with no prior medical history presented with recurrent palpitations. Her baseline 12-lead ECG exhibited normal sinus rhythm with overt pre-excitation. Notably, the precordial leads demonstrated a distinct reverse break sign: a negative delta wave in V1, an abruptly prominent positive delta wave in V2, and a return to a negative delta wave in V3. Echocardiographic evaluation was unremarkable. Based on this specific ECG morphology, a right posteroseptal AP was suspected. An electrophysiological study utilizing 3D electroanatomical mapping (EnSite™ Precision) confirmed the earliest pre-excited ventricular activation at the right inferoposterobasal (posteroseptal) region. Subsequent targeted radiofrequency ablation was successful; the post-ablation ECG showed normal sinus rhythm and the complete disappearance of delta waves. Conclusion: The reverse break pattern is a reliable and easily identifiable surface ECG signature that strongly predicts a right posteroseptal AP. Early recognition of this morphological shift significantly aids electrophysiologists in pre-procedural planning and improves ablation efficiency in anatomically complex regions.

title: Arrhythmias detected by implanted cardiac rhythm recorders in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
summary:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Arrhythmias are a common complication of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM). We sought to characterize the prevalence, risk factors, and prognosis of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM using implantable loop recorders (ILRs).

METHODS: ILRs were implanted in 49 patients with ATTR-CM (84% male; median age, 73.2 [66.2-78.8] years; 71% wild-type, 51% with known atrial fibrillation [AF]). Factors associated with the development of AF or pacemaker implantation were analyzed, and clinical outcomes were compared with those of a contemporary cohort of patients with 125 ATTR-CM without an ILR.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 37.2 [26.6-41.1] months, an advanced conduction disorder (ACD) prompting pacemaker implantation was detected in 16 individuals (33%) and new-onset AF was detected in 17 patients (71% of those without previous AF). Patients with new-onset AF more frequently had wild-type ATTR-CM. Those who needed pacemaker implantation were older and had a higher prevalence of hypertension and right bundle branch block, and a longer PR interval. Compared with patients without an ILR, early detection of arrhythmias by ILR was not associated with a prognostic benefit in terms of survival (P = .57), reduction of syncope (P = 1), heart failure admissions (P = .34), or embolic events (P = .999).

CONCLUSIONS: Although a higher incidence of arrhythmias was identified through ILR monitoring in patients with ATTR-CM, no significant benefits were observed in terms of survival or other hard clinical endpoints. Significant differences were identified in patients who developed new-onset AF and ACD. These differences should be considered during the clinical follow-up of this population.

title: Acute Changes in Left Atrial Appendage Flow Velocity During Pulsed Field Ablation: An Intraprocedural Intracardiac Echocardiography Study
summary: **Background:** Despite the close anatomical relationship between the left pulmonary veins (PVs) and the left atrial appendage (LAA), acute changes in LAA flow during pulsed field ablation (PFA) remain poorly characterized. **Objectives:** To characterize acute intraprocedural changes in LAA flow and transmitral filling during PFA for atrial fibrillation (AF) using paired intracardiac echocardiography (ICE). **Methods:** Patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing PFA were prospectively enrolled if they were in sinus rhythm at the beginning of the procedure. ICE was performed immediately before and after PFA to assess LAA emptying velocity (LAAEv), LAA filling velocity (LAAFv), transmitral E- and A-wave velocities, and E-wave deceleration time (EDT). Paired pre-to-post PFA changes were assessed, followed by a sensitivity analysis using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and exploratory subgroup analyses. **Results:** Among 98 patients, LAAEv increased from 35.45 to 40.00 cm/s immediately after PFA (estimated paired increase, 4.95 cm/s; 95% CI, 2.35-7.80; P less than 0.001), while LAAFv increased by 4.36 cm/s (95% CI, 1.81-6.91; P=0.001). E-wave velocity increased by 8.69 cm/s and EDT decreased by 31.73 ms (both P less than 0.001), whereas A-wave velocity did not change significantly (P=0.08). In the ANCOVA model, changes in heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and vasopressor use were not significantly associated with changes in LAAEv. A marked acute reduction in LAAEv (20% or greater) occurred in 12 patients (12.2%). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. **Conclusions:** LAA flow velocities increased acutely after PFA, accompanied by changes in transmitral filling, although a minority of patients showed a marked acute reduction in LAA emptying.

title: Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia unmasked by beta-blockade in pheochromocytoma presenting as hypertensive optic neuropathy: a case report and literature review
When Swallowing Triggers VT.
summary: We describe a case of swallowing-induced ventricular tachycardia in a young, otherwise healthy male with a structurally normal heart which was refractory to multiple anti-arrhythmic medication and was successfully treated with ablation of a cardiac ganglion in the crux of the heart. We use this case to describe an unusual disease presentation and highlight current evidence related to evaluation and management of ventricular arrhythmias and add to the limited body of evidence related to swallowing induced tachycardia.

title: Evaluation and management of clinically significant arrhythmias in the early neonatal period: a single-center retrospective study of NICU-admitted neonates
summary: Abstract Introduction Arrhythmias in the neonatal period are abnormalities of heart rate that carry a significant risk of mortality and morbidity if not diagnosed early. There is limited evidence on the characteristics, frequency and treatment approaches of arrhythmias in the early neonatal period (0–7 days). Materials and methods In this retrospective study, we analyzed the data of 40 neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)-admitted neonates diagnosed with clinically significant arrhythmias in the early neonatal period between December 2017 and November 2024. Sex, birth weight, clinical signs and symptoms, electrocardiography (ECG), Holter ECG, echocardiography (ECHO) findings, treatment and follow-up outcomes were evaluated. Results Non-benign arrhythmia was detected in 40 (0.97%) of 4126 neonates admitted to the NICU in the early neonatal period. The median follow-up period was 30.5 months (range, 0.25-67 months). The most common arrhythmia type was supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and the most common subtype was atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT). In the bradyarrhythmia group, non-conducted premature atrial contractions (non-conducted PACs) and complete atrioventricular (AV) block were detected. Arrhythmia-induced cardiomyopathy (AIC) was present in eight patients (20%), and congenital heart disease (CHD) was found in five patients (12.5%). Initial treatments included vagal maneuvers, adenosine, amiodarone, and flecainide. One patient died due to heart failure. During the follow-up period, SVT recurrence was observed in four cases, all of whom achieved rhythm control with antiarrhythmic therapy. Conclusions Our study emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in improving the prognosis of clinically significant arrhythmias in the early neonatal period. Non-conducted PACs can be successfully managed with medical treatment when they cause hemodynamic disturbances. These contractions may lead to clinical conditions requiring early intervention, and appropriate treatment can improve cardiac function. The low recurrence and mortality rates in patients without complex congenital heart disease in our study group suggest that arrhythmias in the early neonatal period may have a favorable prognosis with correct diagnosis and treatment. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Cardio-respiratory-gated proton pencil beam scanning for cardiac ablation: workflow and end-to-end validation
summary: Background Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radiotherapy (STAR) offers a non-invasive alternative for ventricular tachycardia ablation, yet motion management remains a critical challenge. While respiratory gating is established, cardiac gating requires a dedicated workflow and gating device. Methods This study establishes and validates an end-to-end workflow for cardiorespiratory gated proton STAR in six healthy swine. Key innovations include a novel pencil-beam scanning (PBS) controller enabling mid-spot beam pausing and resumption, and the integration of CardioKit, an ultrasound-based image-guidance system for real-time soft-tissue tracking. The workflow was evaluated by comparing single-gated (respiratory only) and dual-gated (cardiorespiratory) delivery strategies, assessing system latency, dosimetric accuracy on dynamic phantoms, and motion tracking fidelity against 4D-CT benchmarks. Results The upgraded PBS system demonstrated a gate response latency of <550 µs, effectively mitigating interplay effects in dynamic phantom measurements through gated beam deliveries. CardioKit provided respiratory motion traces highly correlated with 4D-CT data (Pearson r > 0.97) and responded to arrhythmic events within 5 ms. In vivo , dual-gating restricted delivery to the diastolic window (70–100% R–R), which resulted in a reduction in the Internal Target Volume (ITV) expansion by a mean of 45% compared to single-gating (19% vs. 64%), thereby substantially sparing healthy myocardium. Although dual-gating increased total beam-on time, the mid-spot interrupt capability ensured robust dose accumulation without treatment aborts. Conclusion The workflow for imaging, treatment planning, and cardiorespiratory-gated beam delivery was viable for treating all six subjects. The PBS system responded to gating commands < 550 µs and CardioKit responded to irregularities in heartbeat in <5 ms. Cardiorespiratory gating enabled an average 45% reduction in target expansion due to cardiac motion. Comparison of CardioKit respiratory motion traces with respiratory 4D-CT yielded differences of 1.1-1.4 mm in total motion amplitude and 0.97-0.99 Pearson correlation factor. These findings are valuable for establishing a workflow for cardiorespiratory-gated STAR treatment with CardioKit.

title: Distal-to-Proximal Conduction System Ablation as a Bailout Strategy in Refractory Multi-Exit Purkinje-Related Premature Ventricular Contractions and Ventricular Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Ablation of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) originating from the Purkinje network-particularly those with multiple exit sites and morphologies-poses a significant clinical challenge. In refractory cases where conventional ablation fails, proximal conduction system ablation may represent a viable alternative strategy.

OBJECTIVE: to evaluate the safety and efficacy of proximal conduction system ablation in patients with refractory multi-exit Purkinje PVCs with diverse morphologies.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included consecutive patients with drug-refractory, symptomatic Purkinje PVCs who underwent proximal conduction system ablation. Multiple exit sites and morphologies were observed during mapping and ablation, indicating complex activation within the Purkinje network.

RESULTS: Among the 22 patients included, 14 (63.6%) had PVC-triggered ventricular fibrillation. Acute elimination of the PVC by distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation achieved in 21 patients (95.5%), while one procedure (4.5%) was discontinued at the patient's request due to the anticipated risk of conduction system injury. The initial site of earliest activation arose from the posterior fascicle in 63.6% (n=14), the septal fascicle in 22.7% (n=5) and the anterior fascicle in 13.6% (n=3). During ablation, all patients demonstrated a shift in the site of earliest activation. Conduction disturbances occurred in 5 patients (22.7%). During a median follow-up of 32.3 months (IQR 17.5-54.5), one patient (4.5%) experienced PVC recurrence requiring repeat ablation; however, no patient experienced recurrent ventricular fibrillation.

CONCLUSION: Distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation can be an effective bailout strategy for patients with refractory multi-exit fascicular/Purkinje-related PVCs and recurrent VF. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm its long-term safety and efficacy.

title: Mitral Valve Prolapse and Ventricular Arrhythmia Risk in TTN-Mediated Cardiomyopathy: A Single Center Experience.
Prognostic Impact of Ventricular Arrhythmia Timing in Acute Coronary Syndromes Treated with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) often complicate acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The prognostic impact of VA timing relative to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic significance of VA based on their timing of occurrence in relation to PCI.

METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting all-cause mortality with and without VA (sustained or hemodynamically unstable VT/VF) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. The endpoints analyzed were short-term (30 days/in-hospital) and long-term (1 year) mortality. A network meta-analysis comparing VA-before PCI, VA-during PCI, and VA-after PCI with the group not experiencing VA as a reference was conducted.

RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 49,963 patients were included, of whom 3,475 (7.0%) experienced VA. VA was associated with increased short- (OR 5.04, 95%CI 3.78-6.72) and long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95%CI 2.20-3.86). In patients alive at discharge/30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not differ between those with and without VA (OR 0.97, 95%CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis showed that all VA timings are associated with a significantly higher risk compared with the group not experiencing VA. Sensitivity analysis found that VA-after is associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier VA (OR 3.37, 95%CI 1.46-7.82).

CONCLUSIONS: VA substantially increase the risk of death in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Mortality risk emerges to be associated with the timing of VA occurrence, with VA-after PCI associated with the highest risk. These findings highlight the prognostic relevance of arrhythmic events across the entire peri-procedural window, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification.

title: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy is an electrocardiographic pattern characterized by a regular alternation of two distinct cardiac events. It can arise from normal operation of device algorithms or indicate underlying dysfunction, such as sensing abnormalities. Accurate differentiation is crucial to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate clinical intervention.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically elucidate the mechanisms underlying pacemaker-associated bigeminy and establish a practical diagnostic framework.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of six patients exhibiting pacemaker-associated bigeminy on ambulatory electrocardiograms (ECGs). The patients were identified from the databases of the Children's Hospital of Soochow University and the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between March 2020 and December 2025.

RESULTS: We delineate six distinct mechanisms: 1) Non-competitive atrial pacing (NCAP) triggered by sinus tachycardia; 2) Fusion beat exclusion due to evoked response (ER) undersensing; 3) Auto capture (AC) operation with start-stop pattern constrained by maximum tracking rate (MTR); 4) Window of atrial rate acceleration detection (WARAD) activation by non-conducted atrial premature complexes; 5) A Pace on Premature Ventricular Contraction (A Pace on PVC) triggered by PVCs; and 6) Dynamic atrioventricular (AV) delay operation following atrial premature beats.

CONCLUSIONS: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy represents a spectrum of phenomena driven by specific "algorithm-rhythm interactions." Recognition of these characteristic patterns is essential for correctly distinguishing normal device function from malfunction, thereby guiding appropriate clinical management and optimizing patient outcomes.

title: Profound sinus bradycardia preceding ventricular tachycardia storm during emergence from anesthesia in a patient with a prior inferior myocardial infarction: a case report
summary: Abstract Background Ventricular tachycardia (VT) storm during emergence from anesthesia is rare. The significance of a persistent rhythm abnormality after treatment of profound intraoperative bradycardia is uncertain. Case presentation A 60-year-old hemodialysis patient with prior inferior infarction and preserved ejection fraction underwent toe disarticulation. Near the end of surgery, the heart rate fell to about 25 beats/min, with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction. Atropine restored the rate, but not stable sinus rhythm. Five minutes into emergence, monomorphic VT storm began, with no preceding rise in heart rate, blood pressure, or bispectral index. VT persisted or recurred and required multiple shocks; angiography showed patent grafts. The patient survived neurologically intact. Conclusion Heart rate increased after atropine and blood pressure remained stable, but an abnormal rhythm persisted before VT storm developed during emergence. A persistent unexplained rhythm abnormality after treatment of profound bradycardia may warrant rhythm reassessment before emergence.

title: High-Grade Atrioventricular Block and Recurrent Cardiac Arrest in Suspected Isolated Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac sarcoidosis may cause advanced atrioventricular block, ventricular dysfunction, and sudden cardiac death. Isolated cardiac presentations are diagnostically challenging when histologic confirmation and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography are unavailable.

CASE SUMMARY: An 18-year-old woman with recurrent syncope developed high-grade atrioventricular block and recurrent brady-asystolic cardiac arrest requiring temporary transvenous pacing. Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated regional septal thickening, basal to midseptal midmyocardial late gadolinium enhancement and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 38.9%. No extracardiac sarcoid pattern or biopsy target was identified. Giant cell myocarditis and inherited cardiomyopathy remained important alternative diagnoses. She received corticosteroid therapy and subsequently underwent cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac sarcoidosis should remain a diagnostic consideration in young patients with malignant conduction disease and inflammatory cardiomyopathy, while important mimics must be actively considered.

title: Cardiac screening in the young for the detection of cardiovascular disease and prevention of sudden cardiac death.
summary: Sudden cardiac death in the young is often due to silent inherited cardiac conditions. Although evidence increasingly supports cardiac screening as a preventative strategy, policies and frameworks differ globally. Structured screening frameworks that utilise AI-enabled technologies show great potential for enhancing disease detection and risk prediction.

title: Prolonged QT Interval in Hospitalized Internal Medicine Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Determinants and Reversibility.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: QT interval prolongation is a common electrocardiographic abnormality in hospitalized patients, associated with malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Its determinants in internal medicine, and the reliability of correction formulas used to identify it, remain insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including 277 patients hospitalized with QTc prolongation - defined by Bazett correction (QTcB >450 ms in men; ≥460 ms in women) - between January 2016 and December 2023. QTc was independently calculated using Bazett (QTcB) and Framingham (QTcF) formulas, and agreement between the two was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression (complete-case analysis) explored predictors of QTcF-confirmed prolongation, and reversibility was assessed by repeat ECG performed after correction of the underlying reversible cause, or within 72 hours when no such cause was identified.

RESULTS: Mean age was 59.2 ±17.2 years, with a slight female predominance (54.2%). Only 78 patients (28.1%) had QTcF-confirmed prolongation despite all meeting QTcB inclusion criteria. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +31.7 ms between QTcB and QTcF (SD 18.9; 95% limits of agreement: -5.3 to +68.7 ms), strongly correlated with heart rate (r=0.92, p<0.001): the overcorrection increased from +3.6 ms at heart rate <70 bpm to +64.4 ms at >110 bpm. QTcB normalized on the follow-up ECG in 68.2% of patients. In a complete-case multivariable model (n=96 with available serum bicarbonate), no variable reached conventional statistical significance; serum bicarbonate (OR=1.121 per mmol/L; 95% CI: 0.991-1.268; p=0.069) and hypertension (OR=2.522; 95% CI: 0.875-7.275; p=0.087) showed borderline associations with QTcF-confirmed prolongation. In an exploratory analysis of the diabetic subgroup (n=148), peripheral neuropathy (DN4 ≥4) was associated with a 15.8 ms higher mean QTcB (age-adjusted 95% CI: 4.7-27.0 ms; p=0.006).

CONCLUSION: Bazett's formula substantially and heart-rate-dependently overestimates QT prolongation compared with the Framingham formula, a discrepancy now precisely quantified. QT prolongation in hospitalized internal medicine patients is predominantly acquired and reversible. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy was associated with higher QTcB values in an exploratory analysis. Serum bicarbonate showed only a non-significant trend toward association with QTcF-confirmed prolongation after complete-case multivariable adjustment; this hypothesis warrants confirmation in prospective studies with complete acid-base characterization before any clinical application.

title: Prognostic value of the inflammatory burden index in predicting 1-year mortality in patients undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy for heart failure
Beyond the light-driven pacemaker: the suprachiasmatic nucleus as a dynamic coordinator of environmental cues
Transvenous Lead Extraction Without Dedicated Surgical Back up in Low-Risk Patients.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) is associated with major complications that could require immediate surgical rescue. These procedures are performed in an EP lab or hybrid OR with the presence of a surgical team on standby. We have designed an institutional protocol that permits performance of TLE in low-risk situations, in an EP lab without dedicated surgical back-up.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate outcomes of TLE in low-risk patients METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients who underwent low-risk TLE at Emory Healthcare between 2010-23. Low-risk TLE were defined as an extraction of a pacing or ICD lead with a dwell time >= 1 and <= 5 years or a lead < 1 year that required extraction tools.

RESULTS: Among 482 patients who met the criteria, the average lead age was 2.8 ± 1.2 years. The mean number of targeted leads per patient was 1.6±0.7. Extraction tools were required in 33.1% of cases. Major complications occurred in 0.83% of patients (n=4): 2 pericardial effusions requiring pericardiocentesis, 1 pneumothorax and 1 death from cardiogenic shock in an end stage heart failure patient. The patients with pericardial effusions and pneumothorax were part of a procedure that required lead revisions and the insertion of 1 or more new leads. No patients required surgical rescue.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that, in selected "low-risk" patients, TLE can be performed safely in an experienced EP lab at centers with on-site cardiac surgery but without a dedicated surgical standby team, potentially reducing resource utilization in resource-limited healthcare environments.

title: Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population.

METHODS: Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events.

RESULTS: The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type.

CONCLUSION: The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

title: [Psychotherapeutic interventions for reducing stress in patients with cardiac arrhythmias].
summary: Cardiac arrhythmias may remain asymptomatic, but they can also be experienced as palpitations or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) shocks that feel existentially threatening. Even harmless arrhythmias can trigger intense anxiety reactions, including traumatic processing. Therefore, in addition to cardiological diagnostics and treatment, an integrative psychocardiological perspective is needed. From a cardiological point of view, the symptom burden should be reduced, for example, by avoiding substances that promote arrhythmias, treating underlying diseases, and-particularly in ICD patients-optimizing potassium levels. Psychoeducation is central: patients should understand why extrasystoles may be experienced as missed beats, strong palpitations, or a sensation of the "heart beating up into the throat." Equally important is discussing the vicious circle of anxiety: tension, worry, and self-monitoring lower the threshold for perception; perceived cardiac symptoms then intensify anxiety and autonomic arousal. Since these signals are interoceptive, avoidance is not possible, and patients should be taught routines that help them break out of the anxiety cycle. Special attention should be given to patients after an ICD shock or cardiac arrest. They may develop posttraumatic stress disorder induced by the cardiac event (CDI-PTSD). Supportive communication, realistic hope, and basic psychosomatic or psychocardiological interventions can reduce nocebo effects and anxiety spirals. In addition, this approach may help identify patients whose need for treatment should be discussed within a "Psycho-Cardio-Team" that still needs to be established.

title: Conduction System Pacing Versus Biventricular Pacing for Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is an emerging alternative to biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded divergent results, creating uncertainty about the comparative effectiveness.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CSP with BVP for CRT, searching PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through May 2026 (updating a prior review). The primary outcome was change in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF), analyzed with random-effects models and prediction intervals.

RESULTS: Eight parallel-group RCTs including 799 patients (396 CSP, 403 BVP) were included. Pooled ΔLVEF did not differ significantly (MD +2.40%, 95% CI -0.49 to 5.29, p = 0.091; I 2 = 75%). CSP showed a non-significant trend toward shorter paced QRS (MD -7.6 ms, p = 0.14) and improved NYHA class (SMD -0.33, p = 0.12). Heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.69), mortality (RR 1.17), complications (RR 0.84), and procedure time did not differ. The four trials enrolling exclusively LBBB patients favored CSP (MD +5.00%, 95% CI 3.01 to 6.98, p = 0.004; I 2 = 0%), consistent in the three using confirmed LBBAP/LBBP (MD +5.37%, 95% CI 3.23 to 7.52, p = 0.008; I 2 = 0%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of randomized trials of CRT, no statistically significant difference was observed between CSP and BVP for any outcome. Because no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and the clinical-event analyses were underpowered, these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence or comparable safety. Exploratory analyses suggest that patients with LBBB undergoing LBBAP/LBBP may derive incremental benefit, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.

METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).

RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.

CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

title: Evaluation of Acute Electrical and Hemodynamic Improvement During Left Bundle‐Branch Area Pacing Modalities for Resynchronization Therapy
summary: Background While cardiac resynchronization therapy is effective in dyssynchronous heart failure, suboptimal response remains frequent. The acute hemodynamic profile of different left bundle‐branch (LBB) area pacing modalities is poorly defined. Moreover, atrioventricular optimization guided by QRS duration (QRSd) may not yield the greatest hemodynamic benefit. Methods Twenty‐four patients with heart failure, reduced ejection fraction, and LBB block underwent sequential testing of right ventricular septal pacing, left ventricular septal pacing, nonselective LBB pacing, and selective LBB pacing during cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation in a prospective, within‐subject physiological study. At each modality, electrical end points were QRSd and vectorcardiographic QRS area; hemodynamics were assessed with beat‐to‐beat systolic blood pressure (SBP). The atrioventricular interval producing maximal SBP improvement was compared with that producing the narrowest QRSd. Results LBB area pacing modalities significantly reduced QRSd , compared with right ventricular septal pacing (nonselective LBB pacing, 114.0±16.8 milliseconds; selective LBB pacing , 118.4±14.1 milliseconds; left ventricular septal pacing, 124.6±16.0 milliseconds; right ventricular septal pacing, 144.4±27.6 milliseconds; all P <0.01). At the atrioventricular interval that produced maximized SBP improvement, QRSd remained narrower with LBB area pacing than right ventricular septal pacing, and selective LBB pacing provided the greatest hemodynamic improvement ( ΔSBP 16.3±5.2 mm Hg ), exceeding left ventricular septal pacing (13.5±6.2 mm Hg ) and nonselective LBB pacing (12.8±6.3 mm Hg ; all P <0.05). Across modalities, the atrioventricular interval that maximized ΔSBP was consistently shorter than that minimizing QRSd (mean difference, 18–29 milliseconds). Conclusions Selective LBB pacing yields the greatest acute hemodynamic benefit, and the hemodynamic‐optimal atrioventricular interval is shorter than the electrical‐optimal atrioventricular interval, suggesting that modest atrioventricular interval shortening after electrical optimization may better maximize hemodynamics. Registration URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique Identifier: NCT07032064.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

title: Circadian rhythms in health and disease.
summary: Circadian rhythms, serving as a crucial temporal bridge linking neural activity and pathological biology, are regulated by central pacemaker neurons to maintain cellular homeostasis and coordinate diverse biological processes. Circadian rhythm disruption is closely associated with various diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic disorders, and cancer. Circadian rhythms are controlled by core clock genes, such as BMAL1 and CLOCK, modulating numerous physiological processes, encompassing metabolism, immune responses, neural activity, and hormone regulation. Circadian rhythms disruptions arising from shift work, jet lag, or inconsistent sleep schedules are implicated in both the onset and progression of numerous diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The article highlights how circadian dysregulation alters cellular processes to potentially accelerate disease progression. Circadian disruption results in impaired immune function, further promoting disease development and resistance to treatment. Potential therapeutic applications based on circadian biology, such as chronotherapy and personalized medicine, are also discussed. Recent technological advances, embodied in wearable devices and omics approaches, are increasingly providing deeper insights into circadian biology. Further unveiling the role of circadian in health and disease opens new avenues for tailoring treatment timing to patients' biological rhythms, thereby enhancing therapeutic outcomes across various diseases. By bridging fundamental circadian mechanisms with clinical pathology, this review provides a roadmap for future chronotherapeutic interventions in precision medicine.

title: [Atypical Course of Pacemaker Leads via the Accessory Hemiazygos Vein on Chest Radiography in a Patient with a Hypoplastic Left Brachiocephalic Vein].
Clinically Motivated Redesign of the Pennsylvania State University Child Ventricular Assist Device.
summary: Building on validated in vitro and chronic in vivo testing of the Penn State University (PSU) Child Ventricular Assist Device (CVAD), the four-bladed prototype rotor (Rev 0.0) was redesigned using established analytical and computational methods to improve hydraulic efficiency while preserving hemodynamic performance and biocompatibility. Applying turbomachinery principles at the nominal operating condition (3 liters/minute [LPM], 8,000 revolutions/minute [RPM]), a five-bladed design (Rev 1.0) was created with an ideal inflow angle (β1 = 41.0°) and outflow angle (β2 = 27.4°). In silico simulations of Rev 1.0 across the prototype's operating range (7,000-9,000 RPM, 1-5 LPM) demonstrated an approximately 40% improvement in hydraulic performance. The Rev 1.0 rotor was then evaluated on a benchtop mock circulatory loop using fresh ovine blood, confirming the in silico gains. The normalized index of hemolysis (NIH), measured at two clinically relevant conditions (1.5 LPM and 3.3 LPM, both at ~80 mm Hg), was 0.052 ± 0.054 and 0.047 ± 0.033 mg/dL, respectively, and high-molecular-weight multimers of von Willebrand factor were preserved within normal to borderline ranges. By achieving target flows and pressures at approximately 1,000 RPM lower speeds, the redesign reduces power requirements and enables longer untethered operation, advancing a fully implantable PSU CVAD toward a critical unmet need in pediatric advanced heart failure.

title: Wearable Heart Rate Monitoring in Resource-Limited Healthcare
summary: Cardiovascular disease remains the primary cause of premature mortality in low- and middle-income countries, where structural barriers prevent timely detection of cardiac arrhythmias. Wearable sensing technologies, particularly photoplethysmography-based devices, offer a low-cost pathway toward continuous cardiac surveillance; however, their utility has historically depended on cloud-based inference pipelines incompatible with resource-limited environments. This chapter presents a comprehensive narrative review of the convergence of wearable cardiac monitoring and Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML), examining how compressed neural network models deployed on microcontroller-class hardware enable real-time arrhythmia detection without external connectivity. The review synthesizes evidence on sensing modalities, signal processing pipelines, model compression techniques, hardware platforms, and system-level deployment considerations, with specific attention to population diversity, regulatory context, and long-term sustainability.
journal: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series

title: A study protocol of fasting to provide energy needed to help adults in need of cognitive enhancement (Fasting ENHANCE).
summary:
BACKGROUND: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is defined as a self-perceived reduction in cognitive function and is associated with future cognitive impairment. However, few clinical trials have explored the impact of nonpharmacological interventions in older adults with SCD. Time-restricted eating (TRE) restricts food intake to a daily eating window and has shown improvements in cardiometabolic markers associated with cognitive impairment.

OBJECTIVE: The Fasting to provide Energy Needed to Help Adults in Need of Cognitive Enhancement (Fasting ENHANCE) study is a rater-blinded, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial, designed to evaluate the effects of TRE on cognitive function in overweight older adults with SCD.

METHODS: The study aims to enroll older adults (aged ≥65 years) who are overweight (BMI ≥25 kg/m2) and have SCD without objective impairment. Participants are randomized to either a 6-month TRE or Successful Aging (SA) group. The TRE group is instructed to restrict eating to an 8-h window, and the SA group to maintain current lifestyle behaviors. The primary outcome is change in cognitive function, assessed using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status and Montreal Cognitive Assessment at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Secondary outcomes include physical function, blood biomarkers, and self-reported mood, sleep, and quality of life.

CONCLUSION: The Fasting ENHANCE study protocol outlines the methodology for evaluating the effect of TRE on cognitive and metabolic health in older adults with SCD. Results will inform future nonpharmacological interventions aimed at attenuating cognitive decline.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05732935.

title: Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.

METHODS: This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.

RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.

CONCLUSION: IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

title: Polycystin dysfunction and cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD.
summary: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD) is one of the most common inherited kidney disorders characterized by the progressive formation of renal cysts. It is a systemic disease with significant extra-renal manifestations. Among these, cardiac electrical abnormalities are increasingly recognized as clinically important yet underappreciated contributors to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Beyond cyst formation, pathogenic variants in PKD1 or PKD2, which encode polycystin-1 (PC1) and polycystin-2 (PC2), respectively, interfere with calcium homeostasis, mechanotransduction, and mitochondrial function in both kidney and heart tissues. These molecular changes trigger a cascade of pathological events, including RAAS activation, TGF-driven fibrosis, and oxidative stress, leading to structural and electrical remodeling of the heart. These alterations contribute to cardiac electrical remodeling, manifesting clinically as QT interval and corrected QT (QT/QTc) prolongation, left ventricular hypertrophy, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and other electrocardiographic abnormalities. Despite growing evidence, cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD remain understudied in clinical practice. Early detection of subclinical cardiovascular abnormalities may be facilitated by electrocardiographic monitoring, cardiac imaging, and complementary biomarker assessment. Additionally, findings from iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte models support the translational potential of personalized drug-screening platforms. This review summarizes current evidence linking polycystin dysfunction to cardiac electrical abnormalities in ADPKD by integrating molecular mechanisms with experimental and clinical findings. It also highlights the need for integrated cardio-renal approaches to improve cardiovascular surveillance, risk stratification, and future therapeutic development in ADPKD.

title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
summary:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.

RECENT FINDINGS: Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Biphenyl Derivatives with Therapeutic Potential for Atrial Fibrillation by Synergistically Inhibiting NaV1.5 Late Na+ Current and K+ Current.
summary: To overcome the side effects of conduction block and QT prolongation associated with antiatrial fibrillation (AF) drug dronedarone, a novel class of dual IKr and late sodium current (late INa) inhibitors was developed through computational modeling, chemical modification, and electrophysiological screening. Lead compound 8b retained potent IKr inhibition (IC50 = 1.5 μM) comparable to dronedarone. Crucially, 8b avoided dronedarone's peak INa inhibition while enhancing late INa suppression (IC50 = 2.5 μM) to counteract excessive QT prolongation and avoid conduction block. Compound 8b exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic properties (T1/2 = 5.02 h, F = 110% in mice, p.o.) and high ion channel selectivity. In an ex vivo rabbit heart model of AF, 8b demonstrated antiarrhythmic efficacy. Furthermore, 8b was effective in treating doxorubicin-induced heart failure in mice, a condition where dronedarone shows no therapeutic benefit. Collectively, 8b could serve as a potential new class III antiarrhythmic candidate.

title: Electrophysiological remodeling in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy MYBPC3 R943X mutant in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and modulation by IKto-targeting drugs.
summary: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death, often driven by pathogenic variants in sarcomeric genes such as MYBPC3. The precise electrophysiological mechanisms underlying arrhythmogenesis in HCM, particularly in the context of MYBPC3 truncating mutations, remain incompletely defined, hindering the development of targeted therapies. Here, we leveraged human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) carrying the MYBPC3 p.R943X mutation to systematically characterize action potential remodeling and evaluate the efficacy of ion-channel-modulating drugs.High-throughput optical AP assays revealed that R943X mutant hiPSC-CMs exhibit profound baseline electrophysiological disruption, with a marked reduction in normal AP profiles and increased incidence of pro-arrhythmic morphologies, including AP prolongation, early afterdepolarizations, and delayed afterdepolarizations, compared to isogenic non-diseased controls. Pharmacological profiling demonstrated that NS-5806, a Kv4 channel modulator, exerts a biphasic, dose-dependent effect in non-diseased isogenic control cells and partially restores normal AP morphology in R943X mutants by enhancing repolarizing current and suppressing AP prolongation. In contrast, Acacetin, an ITo and late Na+ current inhibitor, preserved electrical stability in non-diseased isogenic control cells but conferred limited and dose-sensitive rescue in mutants, with higher concentrations exacerbating arrhythmic features. These findings provide direct evidence that targeted augmentation of transient outward K+ current can selectively mitigate mutation-induced arrhythmogenic remodeling in hiPSC-CMs modeling HCM. Our study highlights the therapeutic promise, and challenges, of precision ion-channel modulation in genetic cardiomyopathy and establishes a scalable platform for genotype-guided drug discovery.

title: Congenital Long QT Syndrome Type 2: Delayed Diagnosis After a Decade of Seizure-Like Episodes.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) is typically diagnosed in youth. Recognition in advanced age is rare and may be delayed when arrhythmic syncope mimics epilepsy.

CASE SUMMARY: A 93-year-old man with recurrent convulsive syncope presented with marked QT prolongation, notched T waves, and pause-dependent torsades de pointes/pulseless ventricular tachycardia initiated by premature ventricular contractions. Four years earlier, torsades de pointes had been attributed to mild hypokalemia and famotidine, although QTc interval remained prolonged after correction. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic KCNH2 frameshift variant, confirming congenital LQTS type 2. Advanced age, chronic kidney disease, and bradyarrhythmia likely reduced repolarization reserve. An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was discussed but not pursued after a goals-of-care discussion; leadless pacing was used to reduce pauses, and beta-blocker therapy continued.

DISCUSSION: Congenital LQTS may remain occult into advanced age when acquired factors reduce repolarization reserve.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Persistent QT prolongation after reversible factors are corrected should prompt consideration of congenital LQTS regardless of age.

title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases
summary: Abstract Introduction RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Content This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning. Summary Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs. Outlook Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.
journal: Journal of Basic and Clinical Physiology and Pharmacology

title: Sex Differences in the Associations of Age‐Related Genetic Predisposition With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Cohort Study
summary: Background Polygenic risks for diseases are age‐dependent. However, sex differences in the age‐related association between polygenic risk score and incident atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. Methods A prospective cohort study was conducted using UK Biobank data, including 386 154 participants aged 40 to 69 years, with a median follow‐up of 15.6 years. High AF polygenic risk score was defined as ≥0.858 (top quintile). Cox regression, 10‐fold cross‐validated C‐statistic, Royston's R 2 , and population‐attributable risk percentages were used to evaluate sex‐ and age‐specific genetic effects on incident AF. Results High polygenic risk score was significantly associated with incident AF, and continuous‐age analyses showed that the age‐related trajectories differed across sexes ( P for difference in age‐related trajectories=0.005). In age‐stratified analyses, the association was numerically higher in men aged 40 to 49 years (hazard ratio [HR], 2.76 versus 2.07 in women; Bonferroni‐adjusted P for interaction=0.077), whereas it was higher in women aged 60 to 69 years (HR, 2.22 versus 1.95 in men; Bonferroni‐adjusted P for interaction <0.001). Cross‐validated prediction analyses showed broadly similar age‐ and sex‐specific patterns. Population‐attributable risk of high polygenic risk score gradually declined across age strata in men, whereas it first increased and then decreased in women. Conclusions Age‐related genetic predisposition to AF exhibits distinct sex‐specific patterns, offering a foundation for personalized risk stratification and prevention strategies tailored to age and sex.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

title: Research trends and hotspot analysis of sudden cardiac death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
summary: Background: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common genetic heart disease and a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. This study aims to map the research landscape of Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy -related sudden cardiac death over the past 2 decades using bibliometric methods. Methods: We performed a bibliometric analysis of 712 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (2005–2025). Using Cite Space, we examined publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation patterns, and keyword dynamics. Results: Annual publication output rose markedly, with pronounced accelerations after the 2014 European Society of Cardiology and 2020 American heart association/American College of Cardiology guidelines. The United States led in productivity (203 publications) and network centrality (0.40), while China ranked second in output (123 publications) but exhibited limited international collaboration (centrality = 0.01). Co‑citation analysis indicated that clinical guidelines and risk‑prediction models form the field’ score knowledge base, and five of the ten most cited references were international guidelines. Keyword analysis defined 4 principal thematic clusters disease entity, clinical outcomes, imaging biomarkers, and risk stratification and documented a shift from early mechanistic studies to multimodal risk prediction, followed more recently by artificial intelligence–driven models and targeted pharmacological therapies (e.g., mavacamten). Conclusion: This study provides a systematic, data-driven overview of the knowledge structure and evolutionary trends in Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-related sudden Cardiac death research. The findings underscore the field’ s guideline-driven character, document the rise of AI-based risk stratification, and describe a paradigm shift toward disease-modifying therapies, offering actionable insights for prioritizing future research and informing clinical decision-making.

title: Arrhythmic events and genetic variants as drivers for Takotsubo Syndrome: a patient-specific atrial stem-cell model.
summary: Takotsubo Syndrome (TTS) is an acute, potentially life-threatening condition often complicated by ventricular dysfunction and arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is common in TTS patients and associated with increased mortality. However, the arrhythmic mechanisms, genetic variability underlying TTS, and personalised therapy remain unclear. We generated induced pluripotent stem cell-derived atrial and ventricular cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) from TTS patients and provoked TTS-like events by isoprenaline (Iso) stimulation. Compared with controls, atrial TTS iPSC-CMs exhibited enhanced diastolic sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca²⁺ leak and increased arrhythmogenic potential following Iso exposure. Iso-induced stress further increased systolic Ca²⁺ transient amplitude and reduced phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) activity in TTS iPSC-CMs. Under baseline conditions, atrial TTS iPSC-CMs demonstrated unchanged Ca2+ transient amplitude, reduced diastolic Ca2+, elevated SERCA2 activity with faster Ca²⁺ decay compared to controls, which could be explained by increased phosphorylation of PKA-specific phospholamban S16. In contrast, ventricular TTS-iPSC-CM showed increased L-Type Ca2+ current density, but reduced Ca2+ transient amplitude with increased resting Ca2+ leak and reduced PDE4 activity post-Iso-exposure. In atrial TTS iPSC-CMs, the PDE4 activator MR-L2 restored PDE4 activity, normalised several defects in Ca²⁺ handling and prevented arrhythmias more efficiently than the β-blocker metoprolol. Genetic analyses identified variants in the Ca²⁺ handling genes AHNAK and CASQ2 in TTS. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we generated isogenic rescue and mutation-insertion lines, confirming a causal role of p.P5390T in catecholamine-induced arrhythmogenic phenotypes in atrial TTS iPSC-CMs. Our findings support a mechanistic link between genetic predisposition to an excessive catecholaminergic stress response, dysregulated PDE/cAMP signalling, and atrial arrhythmogenesis in TTS-CMs, identifying PDE4 as a potential therapeutic target in this critical condition.

title: It's about time: modeling circadian regulation of cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.
summary: Cardiac electrophysiology models resolve processes ranging from millisecond-scale ion-channel gating to hour-scale protein trafficking; yet, most do not explicitly represent circadian time. Consequently, ion-channel conductance, autonomic input, body temperature, and clock-regulated gene expression are often treated as fixed parameters or time-invariant inputs, causing simulated cardiac cells to correspond to an implicit and potentially arbitrary biological phase. In vivo, however, these factors vary across the ∼24-h cycle and jointly shape sinoatrial nodal pacemaking, ventricular repolarization, arrhythmia susceptibility, and drug response. In this mini-review, we examine recent efforts to incorporate circadian regulation into computational models of cardiac electrophysiology, including sinoatrial nodal and ventricular myocyte models of pacemaking, arrhythmogenesis, seizure-induced sinus arrhythmias, and drug-induced proarrhythmic risk. We synthesize these studies using a layered "source-transfer-target" organization in which intrinsic and systemic circadian sources act through source-specific transfer processes-including transcription, translation, channel trafficking, receptor-mediated signaling, and direct thermal modulation-to regulate shared electrophysiological targets. Building on this synthesis, we propose a general current-level formulation for incorporating circadian regulation of maximal conductance, channel gating, and ionic driving force into Hodgkin-Huxley-type models. Finally, we identify the experimental, computational, and clinical advances needed to translate these formulations into human-specific, personalized models of cardiac rhythm and arrhythmogenesis, with the long-term goal of enabling circadian-aware cardiac digital twins for time-resolved risk prediction and chronotherapeutic optimization.

title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.

METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.

RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.

CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

Immunohistochemical markers for dating cardiac conduction system injury: current knowledge and forensic implications.
summary: The postmortem timing of myocardial injury remains a major challenge in forensic pathology, particularly when conventional histological methods are insufficient during the early hours after an ischemic insult. We conducted a critical narrative review of immunohistochemical markers for myocardial injury dating, focusing on their biological applicability to the cardiac conduction system (CCS). The search was performed using PubMed and Scopus; no date restriction was applied. Over the past three decades, markers including complement components (C5b-9), cardiac troponins, fibronectin, and connexin 43 have been investigated, with varying degrees of validation, for injury dating in working ventricular myocardium. However, the CCS - comprising the sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, bundle of His, and Purkinje fibers - is a histologically and molecularly distinct tissue that has received remarkably little attention in this context. We highlight fundamental differences in cellular composition, connexin expression profiles, extracellular matrix content, and baseline protein abundance between conduction and ventricular tissue that are likely to significantly alter marker behavior and temporal kinetics. The direct application of ventricular-based immunohistochemical timelines to the CCS lacks empirical support and may lead to forensic misinterpretation. The medico-legal implications are potentially significant, as accurate timing of conduction system injury is relevant to cases of sudden unexplained death, drug-induced arrhythmias, blunt cardiac trauma, and medical negligence litigation. Systematic, tissue-specific validation studies are urgently needed.

A lightweight progressive residual convolutional network for interpretable arrhythmia classification.
summary: Arrhythmia poses a serious threat to human health, necessitating research into automated diagnostic methods. Although advances have been made in arrhythmia classification using deep learning, existing models often suffer from high computational cost and poor interpretability, limiting their clinical applicability. To this end, this paper proposes a lightweight progressive residual convolutional attention network (DResCA). Through the synergistic design of stage-adaptive downsampling and channel attention, this network reduces parameter redundancy while enhancing deep ECG feature extraction. To enhance clinical interpretability, template matching and attention visualization are employed to reveal the key ECG regions underlying the model's diagnoses. Five-class classification experiments on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database demonstrate that the model achieves 98.35% accuracy and 97.99% macro-F1 score while maintaining fewer parameters than mainstream deep learning models. These characteristics provide a practical technical pathway for real-time arrhythmia detection on wearable edge computing devices.

title: Ballistic Drift and Wavefront Breakup of Scroll Waves Induced by Ordered Discrete Bagua Heterogeneity
summary: Spiral waves are ubiquitous topological defects in excitable media, and their dynamics under spatial heterogeneity are critical for understanding biological and physical systems. While previous studies have extensively explored random disorder or continuous gradients, the effect of ordered discrete heterogeneity remains largely unexplored. In this study, based on the Barkley two-variable reaction-diffusion model, we systematically investigate the dynamics of spiral waves driven by a Bagua-configured 3-bit discrete heterogeneity field. We reveal a complete dynamical transition sequence as heterogeneity increases: from regular rigid rotation to directional ballistic drift, and eventually to wavefront breakup and defect-mediated turbulence. Counterintuitively, the ordered discrete Bagua heterogeneity does not induce wave tip pinning (as single obstacles do), nor does it cause random meandering (as random noise does). Instead, due to the eight-fold symmetry breaking of the Bagua configuration, it induces a direction-locked ballistic drift. Through mean-square displacement (MSD) scaling and pinning radius analysis, we quantitatively identify the critical thresholds for the three dynamical regimes. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive phase diagram in the parameter space of heterogeneity strength versus medium excitability, and elucidate the physical mechanism of wavefront breakup via the "stretch-thinning-perforation-detachment" cascade. This study provides a novel paradigm for nonlinear wave instability in discrete ordered heterogeneous media, with significant cross-disciplinary implications for cardiac electrophysiology, neural dynamics, and chemical pattern formation.
